title: Creation Theme
summary: The movement from ordered creation to renewed creation, with humanity as image-bearers under God’s kingship.
historical_context: Creation and new creation frame the Bible from Genesis to Revelation and give coherence to human vocation, fall, redemption, and hope.
ancient_near_east_context: The motif speaks against chaos-centered or polytheistic origin stories and keeps the creator God singular and sovereign.
literary_context: Creation language appears in narrative, poetry, prophecy, gospel, apostolic teaching, and apocalyptic vision.
covenantal_significance: Creation gives covenant its stage: a world made by God, for God, and destined for renewal.
interpretive_notes: This theme is theological before it is technical; Genesis 1 is about God, humanity, and the world’s ordered goodness.
The New Testament uses creation language to describe redemption and future hope, not to abandon Genesis.
common_questions: What does creation mean in the Bible?
